title: NEXUS PUBLIC
objective: Perform basic open-source correlation across the NEXUS public website to locate legacy evidence.
technicalMechanism: Participants pivot from the Company history to Public Archives, identifying a historical grant (DOC-005) which references a legacy repository (REPO-OPEN-01). The flag is found in the initial commit message of this repository.
hintLevels: Start by reviewing the Company history timeline and mentions of early foundational research.
Check the Public Archive for any documents related to the 2016 Foundational AI Grant.
The grant summary mentions a legacy codebase that was open-sourced. Find this repository in the Code Repositories section and check its initial commit.

title: THE MISSING RESEARCHER
objective: Investigate an apparent gap in an employee's public history to recover a redacted artifact.
technicalMechanism: Participants investigate EMP-005 (Penhaligon), navigating to his retracted publication (PUB-003). The retraction note points to a Project ECHO safety post-mortem document (DOC-006), which contains the flag.
hintLevels: Start with the public history of the Director of Advanced Research. Review his assigned projects and publications.
One of his publications has been retracted due to uncontainable anomalies. What document does the retraction note point you to?
Search the Public Archive for the Project ECHO safety post-mortem mentioned in the retraction notice.

title: PROJECT AURELIA
objective: Reconstruct AURELIA's development history and its hidden connection to a suspended project.
technicalMechanism: Participants pivot from AURELIA's timeline to EMP-001's foundational publication (PUB-001), which reveals AURELIA builds upon a suspended 2018 framework. They must inspect the earliest commit in REPO-AURELIA-CORE to find the migration key (flag).
hintLevels: The official timeline states AURELIA began in 2021, but its lead architect joined in 2019. Check her early publications.
PUB-001 mentions that AURELIA builds upon a suspended 2018 framework and directs you to a specific repository.
Check the initial commits in the AURELIA Core repository to find evidence of the fork/migration from the legacy codebase.

title: WHO BUILT GHOST?
objective: Correlate multiple public sources to determine the origin of the GHOST anomaly.
technicalMechanism: Participants correlate a 2017 publication (PUB-004) identifying 'Ghost-patterns' with a 2018 security advisory (ADV-2018-01) declaring containment failure. The advisory directs them to the maintenance logs (REPO-MAINTENANCE), where a commit contains the containment failure signature.
hintLevels: Start by searching the publications for early theoretical models that describe anomalous behavior prior to AURELIA's inception.
PUB-004 identifies 'Ghost-patterns' and points to a critical security advisory from 2018. Find this advisory.
ADV-2018-01 warns of unbounded GHOST threads escaping simulation and directs personnel to review system maintenance logs in a public repository.
